summary: All PASS/FAIL checks pass (table below): the age bookkeeping reproduces the existing re-entry and exit counts exactly, the pooled age-1 re-entry hazard equals Type 1, ρ from 1/|a| matches the histogram within 2% away from caustics, and adding Parts 1/2/4 to the MATLAB script leaves every existing output bit-identical (Octave, annealed, 13 cycles). The MATLAB port gives the same numbers as Python on identical kicks.

Kaplan log-normal tail test (4C), reproduced first: annealed predicted α²/2v = 0.0724 vs measured 0.1088 (seed 0 earlier: 0.072 vs 0.10–0.11), quenched 0.0319 vs 0.0266 (earlier 0.032 vs 0.026). Over 10 seeds: annealed 0.0717 ± 0.0014 vs 0.1085 ± 0.0018 — the low-S tail decays 1.5× FASTER than the log-normal predicts; quenched 0.0370 ± 0.0061 vs 0.0332 ± 0.0070 (0.90×); cosine 0.0125 vs 0.0210.

Why annealed misses the log-normal (4D): the annealed run is, parcel by parcel, an i.i.d. product of step Jacobians. The i.i.d. model (10⁷ samples) reproduces the growth rates and the decay of P(S ≤ 2) (0.1090 vs 0.1085 ± 0.0018), with P(S ≤ s, N) within 2.5 standard errors of the 10-seed mean (ratio 0.96 at N = 20, 0.98 at N = 60; the i.i.d. values run 2–7% low at N ≥ 40). The generalised Lyapunov exponent has the plateau large-deviation theory predicts for a quantity bounded below (σmax ≥ 1): L(q) is flat to 10⁻³ for q ≤ −2 at −0.101, so −min L(q) ≈ I(0) ≈ 0.10–0.11, while the Gaussian α²/2v = 0.072 sits at the centre of the distribution and underestimates the far lower tail. Near S = 1, P(S ≤ s) ∝ (ln s)² (σmax = 1 is a codimension-2 set): measured P(1.25)/P(2) = 0.097 against (ln 1.25/ln 2)² = 0.104.

Caustics (1A): the exact count on the row0 line grows at 0.242 ± 0.009 /cycle (annealed), its exact line length at 0.242, against Kaplan Eq. (6) α + β/4 = 0.234 ± 0.006 — Eq. (6) holds. Quenched: 0.198 vs 0.185, consistent within the seed spread. Cosine fails it: caustics 0.207, line length 0.176, but α + β/4 = 0.061. In a mixed phase space most of the line sits in regular islands (r ≈ 0) while the chaotic layer carries the growth, so r is not Gaussian and its mean and variance do not predict E[e^r]. A fixed grid of parcels only gives a lower bound on the count (at 512/px it saturates after N ≈ 12), so the counts come from tracking the line exactly as piecewise-affine pieces.

Branches and low stretch (1A-iv): across x, the ray density ρ correlates with the local share of S ≤ 2 (annealed r = 0.25 at N = 20) and more strongly with the local mean of −r (r = 0.73): bright branches are where the line is compressed, and S ≥ e^r makes low-S parcels a subset of compressed ones (P(r ≤ ln 2 | S ≤ 2) = 1 exactly; P(S ≤ 2 | r ≤ ln 2) = 0.110 at N = 30).

Crossing ages (2B): a parcel that leaves the low set comes back within one cycle with probability 0.121 (annealed), 0.128 (quenched), 0.085 (cosine); Kaplan–Meier whole-run return probability 0.283 / 0.330 / 0.366, against naive fractions 0.283 / 0.328 / 0.359 that ignore censoring.

"Returned before → more likely to return" (2C): crude ratios 1.16 (annealed), 1.77 (quenched; earlier 1.8×), 2.57 (cosine; earlier 2.6×). At fixed depth S_{N−1} the effect largely goes away: in (2, 2.5] the ratio is 0.93 / 1.01 / 0.91, and the Mantel–Haenszel ratio adjusted for depth (7 bins) × age is 0.94 / 1.03 / 1.09, while adjusting for age alone leaves 0.98 / 1.34 / 1.60. The excess is a depth effect — returners sit closer to the threshold — not a memory of having returned.

Metric (4E): measuring S with y stretched by f = 0.5, 2, 4 leaves α unchanged in every mode (to < 1%). For annealed it moves P(S ≤ 2) by up to 20% but the tail rates by ≤ 3% (0.107 / 0.108 / 0.105 for f = 0.5, 2, 4 vs 0.109), so 4C is metric-robust there. For cosine the rate itself moves (0.022 / 0.014 / 0.014 vs 0.021): its low-S set lies in regular islands where S grows polynomially, and what counts as S ≤ 2 depends on the metric at every N. Thresholds S_THR = 1.5 / 2 / 3 give annealed rates 0.109 / 0.109 / 0.107.

notes.caustics: Caustics = sign changes of a = ∂x_N/∂x_0 along the line, counted exactly (piecewise-affine line, budget 1.2·10⁷ pieces). α = slope of mean r, β = 2·slope of var r over N = 10..60; growth fitted on ln(count) over N = 10..last exact N.
notes.corr: Bins of 4 px with ≥ 5 parcels; mean over the three launched rows. Spearman uses average ranks.
notes.pooled: Tracers = the MATLAB lattice (seeded every 2 px in the window). Re-entry: at risk = out of the set at N−1, age = N − exit cycle. Exit: at risk = in the set at N−1, age = N − entry cycle, entrants only (the original cohort is separate in 2B).
notes.KM: F(k) = 1 − Π_{j≤k}(1 − h(j)), hazards with < 200 at risk dropped; "whole run" = largest k with ≥ 200 at risk. Naive = share of spells that ended by the end of the run (censoring ignored).
notes.depth: Depth = S at N−1 of the parcel at risk of re-entering. Counts are per seed. Mantel–Haenszel rate ratio over 7 depth bins × age.
notes.4C: α, v = slopes of mean and variance of ln S on the Eulerian window, N = 20..60; measured = slope of −ln P(S ≤ s) over the same N (points with ≥ 10 parcels). Ratio = measured / predicted.
notes.iid: I(0+) from the density of λ = ln S/N at its lowest bin, difference estimator between N = 40 and 60 (removes the prefactor); L(q) the same way.
notes.Lq: For q ≥ 0 the transfer operator on 2048 directions × 301 fp bins gives the exact vector-norm exponent (= σmax exponent). For q < 0, σmax ≥ 1 makes L(q) plateau at −I(0); the Monte-Carlo difference estimator shows it. Large positive q is dominated by rare samples in Monte Carlo.
notes.4E: S_f = σmax(D M D⁻¹), D = diag(1, f): the same dynamics measured with y stretched by f.
notes.4F: Pooled over the three lines. S ≥ e^r always, so P(r ≤ ln 2 | S ≤ 2) = 1 identically.

method: Map. Yc = y + f(x), Xc = x + Tau·(Yc − row0), with f the piecewise-linear interpolant of the kick dp_x (rows = cols = 1920, K = 48, Tau = 0.5, row0 = 960, correlation length 96 px). M = [a b; c d] (rows x, y) is carried exactly by M ← J M, J = [1 + Tau·fp, Tau; fp, 1], det J = 1; S = σmax(M) = (√(t+2) + √(t−2))/2, t = a² + b² + c² + d².

Randomness. rng(s, 'twister') is emulated with MT19937 (seed 0 → 5489), and the stream is consumed in the script's order: per cycle the kick (959 uniforms) and then the dot jitter (2 × 25600). Quenched draws one kick before the loop; cosine uses no random numbers.

Lattices. The map is exactly periodic in y with period cols/Tau = 3840. One Lagrangian lattice seeded every 2 px over a full period (1.84·10⁶ parcels) gives (i) the MATLAB tracer lattice as its window-seeded subset (921,600 parcels; Parts 1B and 2) and (ii) an exact, uniform sample of the Eulerian window by selecting parcels whose y mod 3840 lies in [0, 1920) at step N (Part 4), in O(N) instead of the O(N²) backward sweep. Validated against MATLAB's 1-px Eulerian lattice: P(S ≤ s) and the ln S moments agree to 10⁻⁴.

Lines (1A). Rows row0 and row0 ± rows/8, 8 parcels/px over all x, carried with M from I. Tangent (a, c); r = ln √(a² + c²). ρ(x, N) from the histogram (4 px bins, normalised so ρ = 1 at N = 0) and from Σ 1/|a| at bin centres along resolved segments (check on a 512/px line). Because the kick is piecewise linear, one step is affine inside each 1-px cell, so a is constant on pieces of the line and every caustic is a corner fold; the line is tracked exactly as pieces, cut where they cross integer x.

Crossing ages (2). Per tracer: cycle of last exit, cycle of last entry (0 = original cohort), number of returns and S at N−1. Risk and event counts are accumulated in [crossing cycle × age] arrays (and [returned before × depth × age]), from which every hazard, Kaplan–Meier curve and ratio follows.

Distribution of S (4). log10 S histogram in 0.05-decade bins on 0–13 plus overflow, P(S ≤ s), moments and quantiles of ln S and band shares, per N. The i.i.d. model draws fp from the first differences of 500 fresh kicks (960,000 values) and multiplies 10⁷ independent products to N = 60.
Seeds. 10 seeds per mode, mean ± sd across seeds; figures show ±1 sd bands.
caveats: Seeds ≥ 1 assume MATLAB's rng(s, 'twister') uses MT19937 init_genrand(s) (as numpy RandomState(s); first draw for s = 1 is 0.4170). Seed 0 is MATLAB's documented stream. Kicks agree with MATLAB's to ~10⁻⁷ relative: randpot1d_getFFT takes √|FFT(c)|, and in the Gaussian tail |FFT(c)| ~ 10⁻¹⁴ is round-off that differs between FFT libraries. Individual chaotic parcels can therefore differ at large N; statistics do not.
Cosine mode is deterministic: all 10 seeds are the same run (sd = 0), not independent samples.
Censoring: hazards need ≥ 200 at risk, so the whole-run Kaplan–Meier value is at the largest such age, not at k = 59. The naive fractions ignore censoring and are biased low for long ages.
Part 2 follows material (Lagrangian), Part 4 measures the Eulerian window. The window is half a momentum period and is not invariant, so the two are different populations once parcels leave it.

S depends on the coordinate metric (4E): thresholds such as S ≤ 2 and every probability built on them change with the scaling of y; growth rates (α) do not. Kaplan's test compares rates, but the prefactors behind the measured slopes are metric dependent at finite N.

Caustic counts are a property of the piecewise-linear kick at 1-px resolution (corner folds); with a smooth kick the folds would be smooth and ρ would diverge as d^{−1/2}. Exact counts stop where the line exceeds 1.2·10⁷ pieces (annealed N ≈ 31, quenched ≈ 33–35, cosine ≈ 41–44), so growth rates are fitted over N = 10 up to that point.
"Type 1" is taken as the immediate bounce-back P(in the set at N | left at N−1), counted from consecutive masks; the check verifies the age bookkeeping reproduces it exactly.
Finite N: 4C fits use N = 20..60; the Gaussian prediction is a central-limit statement while P(S ≤ s) probes the far lower tail, which large-deviation theory (4D) governs.
